title: Cell identity through contact and mitosis

series.axis_order: image column=x,row=y; acquired raw fluorescence arrays are row=y,column=x

task: Track three seeded fluorescent cell nuclei through all 10 original microscopy frames (t=0..9, 540×540 pixels). Starting centers at t=0: A=[281.76144578313256, 160.49518072289158], B=[386.0537897310513, 220.9437652811736], C=[354.64638783269965, 209.82509505703422]. Maintain biological identity through motion, neighboring nuclei contact and any mitosis; brightness ordering or nearest endpoint alone may swap identities. Report all A-lineage nucleus centers at t=4 and t=9, B and C centers at t=9, and the first frame where A is represented by two separate daughter nuclei. Use original image x,y coordinates. The free overview shows every frame at reduced scale, with seed rings ONLY at t=0. You may acquire intermediate frames, inspect native intensity, compute classical tracking or call available specialists. This is a small development sequence with real division and close-neighbor motion, not a long-video tracking benchmark; use null for unsupported fields.

selection: Official public 10-frame sample. A is the first labeled disappearing nucleus followed by a visually verified two-daughter split. B/C are the persistent pair with the closest separation and largest relative motion, selected before inference. No synthetic frames, inserted cells or temporal interpolation.
